PaperTitle: Graph Embedding for Mapping Interdisciplinary Research Networks
Abstract: Representation learning is the frst step in automating tasks such as research paper recommendation, classifcation, and retrieval. Due to the accelerating rate of research publication, together with the recognised benefts of interdisciplinary research, systems that facilitate researchers in discovering and understanding relevant works from beyond their immediate school of knowledge are vital. This work explores diferent methods of research paper representation (or document embedding), to identify those methods that are capable of preserving the interdisciplinary implications of research papers in their embeddings. In addition to evaluating state of the art methods of document embedding in a interdisciplinary citation prediction task, we propose a novel Graph Neural Network architecture designed to preserve the key interdisciplinary implications of research articles in citation network node embeddings. Our proposed method outperforms other GNN-based methods in interdisciplinary citation prediction, without compromising overall citation prediction performance.
SummaryAbstract: This work explores various document embedding methods to identify those that can preserve interdisciplinary implications in research paper embeddings. The authors propose ComBSAGE, a novel Graph Neural Network architecture specifically designed to achieve this by being sensitive to local graph structure during message aggregation. This method is evaluated in an interdisciplinary citation prediction task, where it outperforms other GNN-based approaches without sacrificing overall prediction performance.

References.PaperTitle: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientifc Text
References.Authors: Iz Beltagy, Kyle Lo, and Arman Cohan
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP)
References.SemanticInformation: SciBERT is a BERT-based language model fine-tuned on scientific text to create embeddings from paper content. In the main paper, it is used to generate initial document embeddings from concatenated titles and abstracts. This provides a text-based representation foundational for several evaluated methods and is explicitly mentioned as a component in initializing paper embeddings.

References.PaperTitle: A Comprehensive Survey of Graph Embedding: Problems, Techniques, and Applications
References.Authors: H. Cai, V. W. Zheng, and K. Chang
References.Publication: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge & Data Engineering
References.SemanticInformation: This survey paper provides an overview of graph embedding techniques, which aim to represent graph nodes in a low-dimensional vector space while preserving their relationships. It is cited in the main paper to introduce the concept of node embedding within network analysis. This foundational reference helps establish the background for the GNN-based methods explored in the study.

References.PaperTitle: Measuring and relieving the over-smoothing problem for graph neural networks from the topological view
References.Authors: Deli Chen, Yankai Lin, Wei Li, Peng Li, Jie Zhou, and Xu Sun
References.Publication: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artifcial Intelligence, Vol. 34
References.SemanticInformation: This paper addresses the over-smoothing problem in Graph Neural Networks, where node representations become indistinguishable from their neighbors after multiple layers. The main paper cites it to explain a key challenge that its proposed ComBSAGE architecture aims to mitigate. Over-smoothing can particularly hinder the representation of interdisciplinary research by obscuring distinct community signals.

References.PaperTitle: SPECTER: Document-level Representation Learning using Citation-informed Transformers
References.Authors: Arman Cohan, Sergey Feldman, Iz Beltagy, Doug Downey, and Daniel Weld
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
References.SemanticInformation: SPECTER is a document-level representation learning method that leverages citation information to fine-tune text-based transformers, typically initialized with SciBERT. It aims to learn embeddings where cited papers are closer in representation space than non-cited ones. The main paper evaluates SPECTER as a state-of-the-art baseline method for document embedding, comparing its performance in interdisciplinary citation prediction.

References.PaperTitle: Assessing Network Representations for Identifying Interdisciplinarity
References.Publication: Companion Proceedings of the Web Conference 2022 (Virtual Event, Lyon, France) (WWW ’22)
References.SemanticInformation: This work explores how network representations can identify interdisciplinarity and highlights relationships between citation graph substructures and interdisciplinary research. The main paper cites it as a motivation for designing the ComBSAGE method. It suggests that understanding these structural insights can lead to more effective preservation of interdisciplinary implications in embeddings.

References.PaperTitle: The Structure of Interdisciplinary Science: Uncovering and Explaining Roles in Citation Graphs
References.Publication: Complex Networks and Their Applications XI: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Complex Networks and Their Applications, Vol. 1
References.SemanticInformation: This paper investigates the structural characteristics of interdisciplinary science within citation graphs, uncovering and explaining various roles. Similar to reference [5], it informs the main paper's motivation for developing the ComBSAGE method. It emphasizes that specific citation graph substructures are relevant to interdisciplinarity, guiding the design of aggregation functions in GNNs.

References.PaperTitle: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
References.Authors: Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee, and Kristina Toutanova
References.Editors: Jill Burstein, Christy Doran, and Thamar Solorio
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, NAACL-HLT 2019, Minneapolis, MN, USA, June 2-7, 2019, Volume 1 (Long and Short Papers)
References.SemanticInformation: BERT is a deep bidirectional transformer model pre-trained on large text corpora for general language understanding tasks. It serves as the foundational architecture for domain-specific models like SciBERT [1], which is directly used in the main paper for generating textual embeddings of research articles. This reference contextualizes the advanced NLP methods employed for document representation.

References.PaperTitle: Graph embedding techniques, applications, and performance: A survey
References.SemanticInformation: This survey article provides a comprehensive overview of graph embedding techniques, their applications, and performance. The main paper references it to contextualize the broader field of node embedding in network analysis. Graph embedding is a core area of study for the main paper's GNN-based approaches, aiming to represent nodes in a low-dimensional vector space.

References.PaperTitle: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
References.Authors: William L. Hamilton, Rex Ying, and Jure Leskovec
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (Long Beach, California, USA) (NIPS’17)
References.SemanticInformation: This paper introduces GraphSAGE, an inductive framework for generating node embeddings that can generalize to unseen nodes. GraphSAGE learns aggregation functions to combine information from a node's local neighborhood. The main paper uses GraphSAGE (both MEAN and LSTM aggregators) as a primary GNN baseline for comparison, representing a standard message-passing approach.

References.Authors: Thomas N Kipf and Max Welling
References.SemanticInformation: This paper proposes Variational Graph Auto-Encoders (VGAE) for unsupervised learning of graph embeddings. VGAEs leverage latent variables to model graph structure and node features. The main paper cites VGAE as an example of a Message-Passing Graph Neural Network (MP-GNN) architecture, providing context for the class of models it aims to improve upon.

References.PaperTitle: Semi-Supervised Classifcation with Graph Convolutional Networks
References.Authors: Thomas N. Kipf and Max Welling
References.Publication: 5th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2017, Toulon, France, April 24-26, 2017, Conference Track Proceedings
References.SemanticInformation: This paper introduces Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for semi-supervised learning on graph-structured data. GCNs learn node embeddings by aggregating feature information from neighbors through convolutional operations. The main paper cites GCN as another example of a Message-Passing Graph Neural Network (MP-GNN), further illustrating the family of models relevant to its research.

References.PaperTitle: Semantic and relational spaces in science of science: deep learning models for article vectorisation
References.Authors: Diego Kozlowski, Jennifer Dusdal, Jun Pang, and Andreas Zilian
References.SemanticInformation: This paper focuses on deep learning models for article vectorization, aiming to represent research papers in dense vector spaces that preserve semantic and relational similarities. The main paper cites it to define and provide background on 'research paper representation learning' or 'document embedding,' which is central to its objectives. It highlights that such methods rely on NLP and network analysis techniques.

This article highlights the benefits and importance of interdisciplinary collaboration in scientific research. The main paper cites it to underscore the well-established advantages of interdisciplinary research, thereby motivating the development of tools to facilitate such collaborations. This provides crucial context for the value proposition of the proposed embedding methods.

References.PaperTitle: Efcient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
References.Authors: Tomás Mikolov, Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, and Jefrey Dean
References.Publication: 1st International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2013, Scottsdale, Arizona, USA, May 2-4, 2013, Workshop Track Proceedings
References.SemanticInformation: This foundational paper introduces the Skip-Gram model, a highly efficient method for learning high-quality distributed vector representations for words. It is cited as the basis for DeepWalk [15], a graph embedding method used as a baseline in the main paper. The Skip-Gram model's principle of predicting co-occurring items is extended to graph nodes in DeepWalk.

References.PaperTitle: DeepWalk: Online Learning of Social Representations
References.Authors: Bryan Perozzi, Rami Al-Rfou, and Steven Skiena
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 20th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (New York, New York, USA) (KDD ’14)
References.SemanticInformation: DeepWalk is a graph embedding method that learns node representations by simulating random walks and applying the Skip-Gram model. It aims to capture structural proximities within a network by predicting co-occurring nodes. The main paper uses DeepWalk as a baseline method for evaluation, particularly for calculating network distance between citations.

References.PaperTitle: Understanding over-squashing and bottlenecks on graphs via curvature
References.Authors: Jake Topping, Francesco Di Giovanni, Benjamin Paul Chamberlain, Xiaowen Dong, and Michael M. Bronstein
References.Publication: The Tenth International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2022, Virtual Event, April 25-29, 2022
References.SemanticInformation: This paper investigates the 'over-squashing' problem in GNNs, where information flow is hindered in bottleneck regions of a graph, leading to a loss of distinct node representations. The main paper cites this to explain why representing interdisciplinary research, often found in bottleneck structures, is challenging for GNNs. The ComBSAGE method aims to address this by allowing separate aggregation of messages from distinct communities.

This paper discusses the cognitive and practical challenges inherent in engaging with research across different disciplines. The main paper cites it to explain why it is difficult for researchers to broadly interact with interdisciplinary work, thus emphasizing the need for tools that facilitate this discovery. This highlights the real-world problem that the proposed embedding methods aim to solve.

References.PaperTitle: Representation learning on graphs with jumping knowledge networks
References.Authors: Keyulu Xu, Chengtao Li, Yonglong Tian, Tomohiro Sonobe, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, and Stefanie Jegelka
References.SemanticInformation: This paper introduces Jumping Knowledge Networks (JK-Nets), which learn to adaptively select different neighborhood aggregation schemes for each node in a graph. This approach enhances representation learning, especially in heterogeneous networks. The main paper incorporates jumping knowledge connections into its ComBSAGE model to improve performance in low-homophily networks, which are characteristic of interdisciplinary graphs.

References.PaperTitle: Two Sides of the Same Coin: Heterophily and Oversmoothing in Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
References.Authors: Y. Yan, M. Hashemi, K. Swersky, Y. Yang, and D. Koutra
References.Publication: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM)
References.SemanticInformation: This paper explores the intertwined issues of heterophily (nodes connecting across different groups) and over-smoothing (node representations becoming too similar) in GNNs. The main paper cites this work to underscore the challenges of modeling interdisciplinary research, which often involves heterophilic connections and bottleneck structures in citation graphs. These phenomena make effective representation learning difficult for standard GNNs.
